listenings.text: And that brings us to the week ahead. By Thursday the negotiators will have been in the same building for eleven days, which is longer than anybody expected and longer than either side wanted. The mediation has produced one thing so far, a truce that has held for six days, and by the weekend we will know whether it holds for a seventh. Watch the northern crossing on Tuesday. That is the flashpoint, and if the trucks are still waiting there on Wednesday morning the humanitarian side of this collapses before the political side does. Meanwhile, in Washington, the incumbent will be defending a record on foreign policy that half of his own party no longer supports, and by the time the electoral season starts in earnest, that record will have been rewritten at least twice.

If you want to follow the news in English by ear, stop trying to understand it the way you read it. Here is what actually works. First, know the story before you listen. Read two paragraphs about it in your own language, and you have just removed ninety percent of the difficulty, because you are no longer decoding the content and the language at the same time. Second, listen for the proper nouns. Names of people, names of places, days of the week. They are stressed, they are slow, and they are the skeleton of the report. Third, accept that you will miss the connecting words, and understand that this costs you almost nothing, because in a news report the connections are obvious once you have the skeleton. And fourth, listen to the same three minutes twice, on two different days. The second time will feel like a different recording, and that feeling is the only proof of progress you are going to get.

extra_audio.text: Dana asks Braulio whether he had already read about the story before he heard the broadcast. He answers that he had read about it in Portuguese that morning, and that the broadcast was still too fast for him. Dana tells him that by the end of the year he will have listened to about two hundred of those reports, and that the speed will have stopped being the problem. Braulio asks her what he should be listening for in the meantime. She tells him to listen for the names and the days, because they carry the skeleton of the report.
